item.title: Haiti stampede: 30 killed at historic Citadelle Laferrière
item.description: A deadly stampede at Haiti's Citadelle Laferrière on Saturday claimed at least 30 lives as crowds gathered for an annual celebration. Overcrowding and rainfall contributed to the tragedy at the historic fortress, with many young people among the victims. Officials are responding to the scene, and the death toll may increase.

item.title: Pro-Palestine rally: Over 500 arrested in London for protesting
item.description: London police arrested over 500 individuals during a pro-Palestinian demonstration. The arrests were made for showing support for Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the UK. This action follows a High Court ruling that questioned the ban's legality. Organizers criticized the police action, citing the court's decision. The ban on Palestine Action has led to numerous arrests since its inception.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump's peace board faces a cash crunch
item.description: Donald Trump's Board of Peace has secured only a fraction of the $17 billion pledged for Gaza's reconstruction and governance. Despite billions pledged by Gulf Arab states, only three countries have contributed funds, totaling under $1 billion. The ongoing war with Iran has further complicated these funding difficulties.

item.title: Pak military contingent lands in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Pakistan has dispatched a significant military contingent, including approximately 13,000 soldiers and 10-18 jets, to Saudi Arabia. This deployment, part of a strategic defence pact, aims to bolster joint military coordination and operational readiness. The move underscores the mutual defence agreement where an attack on one nation is considered an attack on the other, enhancing regional security.

item.title: Musk accused of 'ambush' ahead of $100bn OpenAI trial
UK pauses Chagos handover deal after Trump criticism
item.description: Britain has shelved plans to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius following strong criticism from US President Trump. The deal, which included leasing Diego Garcia for a century, will not proceed without US support. A former top official indicated the UK government was forced to abandon the plan due to Trump's opposition.

item.title: Under Trump's Nasa, moon rocket from Boeing faces uncertain future
item.description: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully sent astronauts around the moon using Boeing's rocket. However, the Trump administration is now seeking cheaper alternatives from competitors like SpaceX for future lunar endeavors. This move puts pressure on NASA's leadership to deliver on ambitious moon landing goals by 2028, despite the established but costly nature of current programs.

item.title: 'It's OK to howl at Moon': Why Nasa streamed Artemis flight on Twitch
item.description: NASA flight director Zebulon Scoville championed public engagement for the Artemis Moon missions, implementing an optical communications system for higher-resolution streaming. The Artemis II crewed flight saw extensive live programming across NASA platforms and social media, attracting millions of viewers. Astronauts' vivid descriptions and genuine emotion captivated audiences, marking a shift towards a more engaging public narrative for space exploration.

item.title: Vance-led team lands in Pak’s Nur Khan base, same air hub targeted by India during Op Sindoor
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance and an Iranian delegation arrived at Pakistan's Nur Khan airbase for peace talks. This base, a key Pakistani military hub, was reportedly targeted by Indian missile strikes last May. The US delegation's choice of the airbase highlights its strategic importance and proximity to Islamabad, despite past damage.
item.dc:creator: Surendra Singh

item.title: US-Iran direct talks begin in Pakistan amid disputes, distrust
item.description: Direct US-Iran talks commenced in Pakistan Saturday, following a fragile ceasefire. US Vice President JD Vance met with Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf to discuss advancing the peace, amidst ongoing Israeli attacks. Regional powers, including China, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, are present to facilitate discussions on critical issues like compensation for war damages.

item.title: 'Going to have big problems': Donald Trump warns China on reports of weapons shipments to Iran
item.description: Donald Trump asserted US military dominance over Iran, claiming to have dismantled its capabilities and warning China against supplying weapons. Despite ongoing peace talks mediated by Pakistan, Trump declared victory regardless of a deal, emphasizing America's win and control over key shipping routes.

item.title: Milgram’s electric shock experiment: The test that exposed dark side of human obedience to authority
item.description: Stanley Milgram’s obedience experiments revealed how ordinary people could follow authority to disturbing extremes, with many participants administering what they believed were harmful shocks. Inspired by the Holocaust, the study became a landmark in psychology while raising serious ethical concerns. Decades later, its findings remain debated, with critics arguing the results reflect pressure, context, and interpretation as much as obedience.
